theorems.statement: ∀ (K F : Type*) [Field K] [Field F] [Algebra K F] (x : F), Transcendental K x → ∀ q : Polynomial K, q.Monic → Irreducible q → ∃ A : Subalgebra K F, ∀ f : F, f ∈ A ↔ ∃ a b : Polynomial K, ¬ q ∣ b ∧ f = Polynomial.aeval x a / Polynomial.aeval x b
theorems.natural_summary: Define A by the stated fraction predicate. Irreducibility makes q prime, so permitted denominators include 1 and are closed under multiplication. Transcendence ensures their evaluations are nonzero. Constants use denominator 1; common-denominator addition and fraction multiplication establish closure. These properties define a K-subalgebra, whose membership equivalence is definitional. No rational-generation assumption is used.
